question.prompt: For how many integer values of \(x\) is \(|2x| \le 7\pi?\)

solutions.title: Bound the possible even values
solutions.explanation:
Because \(x\) is an integer, \(2x\) must be even. We only need to locate \(7\pi\) between nearby integers. Using \(3<\pi<3.142\),
\[
21<7\pi<7(3.142)=21.994<22.
\]
Thus the even values satisfying the absolute-value bound are exactly
\[
2x=-20,-18,\ldots,-2,0,2,\ldots,18,20.
\]
Their absolute values are at most \(20\), while every other even integer has absolute value at least \(22\).

Dividing by \(2\), the possible values of \(x\) are \(-10,-9,\ldots,9,10\). There are \(10+1+10=21\) values.

The answer is \(\boxed{21}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
